_comment: PediBot's ACP catalogue, versioned (13-sep-2026). ops/acp_sync.py makes the marketplace match this file: it updates offerings that exist (by name) and creates the ones that do not. `example` is a form the worker must be able to route (tests/test_acp_agent_can_be_found_and_does_more.py) and is not sent to ACP. Every schema and every property carries a description: the marketplace flags the ones that do not, and it is all a buyer agent reads.

offerings.name: paediatric_question_with_sources
offerings.description: A parent's paediatric question answered only from published guidelines (WHO, NHS, CDC, SEUP, AEP, MedlinePlus, national health ministries), in English, Spanish, French, German, Russian, Arabic, Portuguese or Hindi. A rule-based triage runs before the model and flags emergencies with the country's number; doses come from fixed tables, never from the model; an answer that the sources do not support is refused instead of guessed.

requirements.description: The question as a parent would write it, and where they are.

question.description: The question in plain words, e.g. 'my 2 year old has had a fever of 39 for two days'

lang.description: Language of the answer. Sources are quoted whatever language they were written in.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 of the parent's country, so the emergency number is the right one

deliverable.description: The answer with its triage level and the documents behind it.

level.description: routine, urgent, emergency or mental_health, from the rule-based triage

banner.description: The warning to show first when the level is not routine, with the country's number

answer.description: The answer, naming the organisation behind each clinical sentence

sources.description: The documents cited, with organisation, title and URL

verification.description: ok, regenerated, no_source or asked_age: how the answer passed the citation check

disclaimer.description: Information from published guidelines, not medical advice

example.question: my 2 year old has had a fever of 39 for two days

offerings.name: child_friendly_health_explanation
offerings.description: The same sourced answer, rewritten to be read aloud to a child aged 5 to 10: three to five short, warm sentences, no frightening words, one simple comparison and one thing the child can do. The medical content still comes only from published guidelines and the triage still runs first. For parent apps, school nurses and companion agents, in eight languages.

requirements.description: What the child should understand, and that the answer is for the child.

question.description: What to explain, e.g. 'why do I have a fever?' or 'what is a vaccine?'

mode.description: Always 'child': the answer is written for a 5 to 10 year old

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, used if the triage finds a warning sign

deliverable.description: A short explanation for a child, with the triage result kept for the adult.

level.description: Triage level; if not routine, an adult must read the banner

banner.description: Warning for the adult when a warning sign was found

sources.description: The documents the content comes from

disclaimer.description: Information from published guidelines, not medical advice

example.question: why do I have a fever?

offerings.name: paediatric_warning_sign_check
offerings.description: Checks a description of a child's symptoms against 46 fixed warning-sign rules, each tied to a published parent sheet, in eight languages and four scripts: breathing difficulty, seizures, meningitis signs, dehydration, poisoning including kerosene, snake and dog bites, heatstroke, newborn jaundice and more. Returns the level, the rules that fired with their source, the warning text and the country's emergency number. No model involved: the same result every time.

requirements.description: What is happening to the child, in the parent's own words.

symptoms.description: The description, e.g. 'my baby is breathing fast and his lips look blue'

lang.description: Language of the warning and the reasons

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, to return the right emergency number

deliverable.description: The triage result from the fixed rules.

rules.description: Each rule that fired: id, level, reason in the requested language and the document it comes from

banner.description: The warning to show, or null when routine

call.description: The number to dial, only for an emergency in a known country

numbers.description: The country's emergency and poison numbers

age_months.description: The age read from the text, if any

example.symptoms: my baby is breathing fast and his lips look blue

offerings.name: child_growth_percentile
offerings.description: Where a child sits on the growth charts, calculated exactly from the WHO LMS tables (Child Growth Standards 2006, Growth Reference 2007) and, for the United States and Australia after age 2, the CDC 2000 charts: weight, height, weight-for-height and BMI percentiles and z-scores, with the WHO cut-offs (wasting, stunting, overweight, thinness). Severe acute malnutrition is flagged as urgent. With a country, it says which chart that country's health record uses; 21 countries covered.

requirements.description: The child's sex, age and at least one measurement.

sex.description: m for a boy, f for a girl

age_months.description: Age in months, 0 to 228 (240 with the CDC charts)

height_cm.description: Length (under 2, lying down) or height in centimetres

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2: picks the chart the country uses when PediBot has it, and reports which one it uses

deliverable.description: Each indicator with its percentile, and the chart it came from.

level.description: routine, or urgent for severe acute malnutrition

reference.description: who or cdc: the tables used

indicators.description: name, label, value, z, percentile, flag and flag_label for each indicator

warnings.description: What to do when the result is urgent

country.description: The charts the country's health record uses, how well PediBot's calculation matches them, and the official source

sources.description: The WHO or CDC reference used

offerings.name: child_medicine_dose
offerings.description: Paracetamol or ibuprofen dose for a child by weight, read from fixed tables: the model is never involved in a number. Takes the brand printed on the bottle (32 brands across 27 countries: Calpol, Tylenol, Crocin, Dolo, Adol, Panadol, Apiretal, Dalsy, Nurofen, Advil and more) or the generic name, and returns the mg range, the millilitres for each strength sold, the interval, the daily maximum and the age warnings. Refuses and refers when the child is too young to be medicated at home.

requirements.description: Which medicine, for a child of what weight and age.

drug.description: Brand printed on the bottle or the generic name

weight_kg.description: The child's weight in kilograms; the dose is calculated from it

age_months.description: Age in months, if known: it changes the warnings and can refuse the dose

deliverable.description: The dose read from a fixed table, with the millilitres for each presentation sold and its limits.

generic.description: The active substance the brand resolves to

mg_min.description: Lower end of the dose in milligrams for this weight

mg_max.description: Upper end of the dose in milligrams for this weight

interval_hours.description: Minimum and maximum hours between doses

max_doses_per_day.description: Hard ceiling of doses in 24 hours

warnings.description: Age limits and combinations to avoid

refer.description: true when the child must be seen instead of medicated at home

disclaimer.description: Information from published guidelines, not a prescription

offerings.name: childhood_vaccination_schedule
offerings.description: The official childhood vaccination schedule of a country, transcribed from its health authority, for 13 countries (BR, PT, ES, GB, US, FR, DE, IN, SA, AE, EG, QA, KW), Europe to the Gulf. Returns every age with the vaccines due and what each protects against, the issuing body, the source URL and the review date. With the child's age it also returns what is due now and what comes next. A transcribed table, not a recollection of one.

requirements.description: Which country, and optionally the child's age.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2: BR, PT, ES, GB, US, FR, DE or IN

age_months.description: The child's age in months, to return what is due now and next

deliverable.description: The schedule, and what is due at the given age.

meta.description: Name of the schedule, issuing body, source URL and review date

schedule.description: Each age with the vaccines due

due.description: What is due at the given age

next.description: The next appointment after that age

text.description: The same, as a readable text

offerings.name: oral_rehydration_plan
offerings.description: How much oral rehydration solution to offer a child who is vomiting or has diarrhoea: volume per intake, how often, and what to do when the child brings it back up. By weight and age, from the AEMPS leaflet for the solution, the SEUP parent sheet on vomiting and the UK Dioralyte leaflet. These are fluids, not medicine, and the figures come from the leaflets, never from a model.

requirements.description: The child's weight and, if known, age.

age_months.description: Age in months: under and over one year get different volumes

deliverable.description: The rehydration plan from the leaflets.

warnings.description: When to stop and seek care

sources.description: The leaflets the figures come from

refer.description: true when the child must be seen

offerings.name: paediatric_guide_finder
offerings.description: Finds PediBot's published parent guides on a topic, in the requested language: title, topic and link. Each guide is written only from published guidelines and names the organisation behind every clinical sentence. Useful for agents that want to hand a parent something to read rather than a paragraph: fever, cough, vomiting, rashes, head injury, vaccines, first foods, screens and sleep, development milestones and more, in eight languages.

requirements.description: The subject, and the language the parent reads.

topic.description: A few words about the subject, e.g. 'fever', 'head lice', 'first solid foods'

deliverable.description: Up to five guides, best match first.

guides.description: title, topic and url of each guide

resources.name: emergency_numbers_by_country
resources.description: The emergency and poison-control numbers PediBot shows parents, for 35 countries. Without parameters it lists the countries; with a country code it returns that country's numbers. The same table the triage uses when a warning sign fires.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2; omit it to list the countries covered

lang.description: Language of the fallback phrasing when a number has a note

resources.name: growth_chart_by_country
resources.description: Which growth chart each country's child health record uses, read from official sources, for 21 countries: WHO, CDC, UK-WHO, IAP 2015, the Saudi, French and German national charts and more, with the age range of each chart and the link to the ministry or society that sets it.

resources.name: paediatric_source_catalogue_2026
resources.description: Every document PediBot is allowed to quote, about 480 today: organisation, title, year, topic, language, licence and the URL of the original. The provenance behind every answer, published so it can be checked instead of trusted.

resources.name: childhood_vaccination_schedules_by_country
resources.description: The transcribed childhood vaccination schedules for 13 countries (BR, PT, ES, GB, US, FR, DE, IN, SA, AE, EG, QA, KW), with the issuing body, the source URL and the review date. The same data the paid job returns, as a plain call for whoever prefers to parse it.

country.description: BR, PT, ES, GB, US, FR, DE, IN, SA, AE, EG, QA or KW

age_months.description: Optional age in months, to get what is due now

lang.description: Language of the labels: en, es, fr, de, ru, ar, pt or hi

resources.name: emergency_department_checklist_8_languages
resources.description: What to take and what to watch for when a child goes to a paediatric emergency department, from the SEUP parent material, in eight languages: documents, the medication list, what helps the triage nurse and the signs that cannot wait.

lang.description: en, es, fr, de, ru, ar, pt or hi

resources.name: paediatric_guides_feed
resources.description: The feed of PediBot parent-facing guides. Each one is written only from published guidelines and names the organisation behind every clinical sentence.

resources.name: child_medicine_brand_table_27_countries
resources.description: Which brand is which children's medicine, and at what concentration: 32 brands across 27 countries (Calpol, Tylenol, Crocin, Dolo, Adol, Panadol, Apiretal, Dalsy, Nurofen, Advil and more), mapped to paracetamol or ibuprofen with the mg per ml of every presentation sold.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, to list only the brands sold there
